Senses.PreferredTarget: the word or saying raised for investigation
Senses.Explanation: The graphs mean “speech” or “a saying” (話) + “head” or “front” (頭). In the corpus passages grouped here, the compound names a word, question, or saying that is explicitly looked at, raised, taken up, remembered, or investigated. Dahui Zonggao says to “look at a saying” (看箇話頭) and immediately supplies Zhaozhou’s exchange, “Does a dog have buddha-nature or not?” (狗子還有佛性也無), answered “no” (無). Elsewhere Dahui says, “When the doubt on the saying is broken, the thousand and ten thousand doubts are broken at once” (話頭上疑破，則千疑萬疑一時破). The corpus also records the assigned contents as Zhaozhou’s word “no,” Zhaozhou’s “cypress tree in the courtyard,” Yunmen’s “a dry shit-stick,” and the question about neither speech nor silence. Hanyue Fazang gives an explicit definition: “What is called a saying is one matter or one thing before the eyes” (所謂話頭者，即目前一事一法也). Attested collocations show the deployment range: “investigate a saying” (參話頭), 187 hits in 76 texts; “look at a saying” (看話頭), 118 hits in 46 texts; “one saying” (一句話頭), 136 hits in 30 texts; “one’s originally assigned saying” (本參話頭), 89 hits in 50 texts; “raise a saying” (舉話頭), 35 hits in 24 texts; “take up a saying” (提話頭), 32 hits in 24 texts; and “the saying of the word ‘no’” (無字話頭), 14 hits in 12 texts. These are among 2,575 occurrences of the headword in 297 allowlisted texts.
Senses.Note: This sense is separated from the ordinary exchange sense because these passages attach the word to explicit instructions to look, raise, take up, remember, recite, or investigate a specified word, question, or saying. The entry keeps those actions in the wording of the records. Counts are allowlist-scoped results from zc.count. The explicit definition is Hanyue Fazang’s statement in The Recorded Sayings of Master Sanfeng Zang (三峰藏和尚語錄); it is reported as his definition and is not silently attributed to the whole corpus.

Occurrences.Kwic: 只就動止處。看箇話頭。便是釋迦老子達磨大師出來也。只是這箇。僧問趙州。狗子還有佛性也無。州云無。
Occurrences.AttributionNote: Dahui’s own record. In an instruction to a lay recipient, he says to “look at a saying” and immediately gives Zhaozhou’s dog question and the answer “no.”

Occurrences.Kwic: 單單提起箇無義味話頭，自最初一日立定脚頭，不得分毫移動，密密與之做向前去
Occurrences.AttributionNote: Zhongfeng Mingben’s Miscellaneous Records, in his address to the assembly at Shunxin Hermitage. He tells the assembly to take up a saying “without the flavor of meaning” and stay with it from the first day.

Occurrences.Kwic: 行住坐臥，單單只提起本參話頭，發起疑情，憤然要討箇下落。
Occurrences.AttributionNote: Boshan’s Admonitions on Chan, in “Admonitions for beginners doing the work.” The text says that while walking, standing, sitting, or lying down, one takes up only one’s originally assigned saying, raises doubt, and seeks where it comes down.

Occurrences.Kwic: 所謂話頭者，即目前一事一法也。
Occurrences.AttributionNote: Hanyue Fazang’s own Extended Record. This is an explicit in-corpus definition: “What is called a saying is one matter or one thing before the eyes.”

Occurrences.Kwic: 令看外道問佛不問有言．不問無言因緣。經三載。一日問曰。汝記得話頭麼。試舉看。
Occurrences.AttributionNote: The Five Lamps Compendium narrates that Yuanjian had the student examine the outsider’s question to the Buddha about neither speech nor silence. Three years later Yuanjian asks, “Do you remember the saying? Try to recite it.” This is biographical narration with teacher and student in one occurrence, so MasterName is null.

Senses.PreferredTarget: a saying, remark, or thread of an exchange
Senses.Explanation: In encounter records, the same compound denotes words spoken in an exchange: a saying, a remark, or the thread being carried by the speakers. A master calls words spoken after a long silence “a fine saying” (好箇話頭); masters ask for “my saying” to be returned (還我話頭來), ask “what does your saying say?” (你話頭道甚麼), or ask where someone obtained “this saying” (這話頭). In the exchange between Sansheng Huiran and Xuefeng Yicun, Sansheng says that the teacher of fifteen hundred people “does not even recognize the saying” (話頭也不識). In the “three pounds of hemp” exchange, Fuyan Liangya says that Dongshan Shouchu supposed Liangya did not understand “his saying” (他這話頭), referring to Dongshan’s answer “three pounds of hemp.” The recurring forms support the range: “return my saying” (還我話頭來), 78 hits in 44 texts; “does not even recognize the saying” (話頭也不識), 185 hits in 87 texts; and “remember the saying” (記得話頭), 68 hits in 61 texts. The records do not assign one further gloss to all of these conversational uses.
Senses.Note: This sense covers the word as a unit within recorded speech rather than as the specified word, question, or saying that someone is told to investigate. Raised cases are left with MasterName null so that a later compiler or commenting master is not substituted for the speakers in the earlier exchange. Counts are allowlist-scoped results from zc.count.

Occurrences.Kwic: 三聖問雪峯。透網金鱗以何為食。峯云。待汝出網來向汝道。三聖云。一千五百人善知識。話頭也不識。峯云。老僧住持事繁。
Occurrences.AttributionNote: Dahui raises the earlier exchange between Sansheng Huiran and Xuefeng Yicun and then comments on both speakers. Because the occurrence is a raised case, MasterName is null; the words “does not even recognize the saying” belong to Sansheng in the quoted exchange.

Occurrences.Kwic: 上堂。良久曰。好箇話頭。若到諸方。不得錯舉。便下座。
Occurrences.AttributionNote: The Five Lamps Compendium, in the section for Yunmen Xianqin. After a long silence, Xianqin says, “A fine saying; if you reach other places, do not recite it wrongly,” and steps down. Xianqin is not present under a verified canonical spelling in the project roster, so MasterName is null.

Occurrences.Kwic: 問。一口吞盡時如何。師曰。我在你肚裏。曰。和尚為甚麼在學人肚裏。師曰。還我話頭來。
Occurrences.AttributionNote: The Five Lamps Compendium, in Yunmen Wenyan’s section. In a direct exchange, Yunmen answers the follow-up with “Return my saying to me.” The surrounding section also contains his answers “the autumn wind reveals the body,” “a dry shit-stick,” and “the eastern mountain walks on the water.”

Occurrences.Kwic: 僧出問。如何是佛。山答曰。麻三斤。參罷。山至寮謂師曰。我今日答這僧話。得麼。曰。恰值某淨髮。山曰。你元來作這去就。拂袖便出。師曰。這老漢將謂我明他這話頭不得。
Occurrences.AttributionNote: The Five Lamps Compendium, in the section for Fuyan Liangya. The passage distinguishes Dongshan Shouchu, who answers “three pounds of hemp,” from Liangya, who later calls that answer “his saying.” The occurrence contains two speakers and Liangya lacks a verified project-roster spelling, so MasterName is null.

Occurrences.Kwic: 僧問。不離生死而得涅槃。不出魔界而入佛界。此理如何。師曰。赤土茶牛嬭。曰。謝師答話。師曰。你話頭道甚麼。僧擬議。師便喝。
Occurrences.AttributionNote: The Five Lamps Compendium, in Yuantong Faxiu’s section. After the monk thanks him for answering, Faxiu asks, “What does your saying say?” This is Faxiu’s direct exchange, not a raised case.
